headline: Former Hartwell Building Maintenance Worker Breaks 20-Year Silence
subheadline: Retired employee speaks in riddles, references 'the other blueprints' before interview ends abruptly
summary: A former Hartwell Building maintenance worker has come forward with cryptic statements about his time working for Omnicorp Holdings, though he refuses to speak plainly about what he witnessed.
content:
Gerald Voss worked maintenance at the Hartwell Building for 23 years before his sudden retirement in 2004. Last week, he agreed to speak with reporters for the first time.

The interview, conducted at a diner eight miles from the building, lasted exactly 47 minutes before Voss abruptly left.

"There are blueprints they show the city," Voss said, stirring his coffee without drinking it. "And there are blueprints they don't. I've seen both. I wish I'd only seen one."

When asked to clarify, Voss would only shake his head. "You're asking the wrong questions. Don't ask what's on Floor 13. Ask why the building needs Floor 13. Ask what happens to the water pressure every night at 3:47 AM. Ask why they replaced all the mirrors on Floor 7 eight times in twenty years but the reflections stay the same."

Voss claims he was part of a four-person maintenance team, but says he's the only one who "got out clean." He declined to elaborate on what happened to his colleagues, except to say they "work for Omnicorp directly now" in positions he "couldn't describe if he wanted to."

The most unsettling moment came when asked about the building's 1923 construction.

"1923," Voss repeated, laughing without humor. "Is that what the records say? Check the foundation stones. Really look at them. There's writing that predates this city by... well. That's not my story to tell."

Omnicorp Holdings responded to a request for comment with a single sentence: "Mr. Voss's employment records indicate a satisfactory tenure and a voluntary retirement. We wish him well."

Voss has since disconnected his phone. Neighbors report he's placed aluminum foil over all windows facing the direction of downtown, where the Hartwell Building stands 8.47 miles away.
author: Tom Hendricks, City Hall Reporter
